title: Bank of China Colombo branch launches as Sri Lanka’s first RMB clearing bank | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:19
-     - 189

Bank of China Colombo branch unveiled Sri Lanka’s first RMB clearing bank last week. From left: Chinese Ambassador Wei Huaxiang, CBSL Deputy Governor K.G.P. Sirikumara, Finance and Planning Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando, and Bank of China President Zhang Hui – Pic by Upul Abayasekara

Bank of China Colombo branch last Thursday became Sri Lanka’s first renminbi (RMB) clearing bank, formally launching operations that allow trade and investment with China to be settled directly in the Chinese currency, rather than through the US dollar.

The branch was authorised as a clearing bank by the People’s Bank of China (PBOC), China’s central bank. Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) Deputy Governor K.G.P. Sirikumara said the move would strengthen the connection between Sri Lanka’s banking system and China’s financial system. He cautioned, however, that the facility’s benefits hinge on how widely it is adopted.

“The success of this initiative will depend not only on establishing the facility, but also on how widely it is used,” Sirikumara said at the launch.

An RMB clearing bank is a lender designated by the PBOC to process, clear, and settle RMB transactions outside mainland China.

Until now, local lenders handling RMB went through banks in China. “Previously, domestic interbank RMB transfers in Sri Lanka generally had to be routed through correspondent bank accounts in China. This could involve additional processing time and intermediaries,” Sirikumara said.

Banks and businesses can now maintain RMB accounts with the clearing bank, make cross-border RMB payments with China, and settle RMB payments locally. He said this was expected to improve efficiency, lower transaction costs, and make transfers more convenient. Importers also stand to avoid converting rupees into US dollars and then into RMB, a process CBSL Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe has said raises costs and exposes traders to multiple exchange rate risks.

The potential gains are significant given the scale of trade with China, Sri Lanka’s largest source of imports. Imports from China totalled $ 5.15 billion in 2025, up 16% year-on-year, while exports rose 10% to $ 279 million, according to Export Development Board data. Sirikumara said RMB settlement could simplify payment arrangements and open access to a wider range of RMB banking and financing services. Over time, he said, it could also support greater trade and investment.

He also pointed to a potential link with China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS), which processes cross-border RMB payments through standardised payment messaging and settlement arrangements. He said the clearing bank could help Sri Lankan financial institutions explore access to it. Former Chinese Ambassador Qi Zhenhong told an earlier RMB Internationalisation Forum in Colombo that the CIPS had 1,729 participants, covering over 5,000 licensed banking institutions across 189 countries and regions. Sirikumara said the idea of an RMB payment facility between the two countries was first discussed at that forum.

Sirikumara called on commercial banks to engage with the clearing bank, explore its services, and build awareness among customers. He also urged importers and exporters to assess whether settling in RMB would be suitable and cost-effective for their businesses. The CBSL will work closely with the PBOC, Bank of China, and licensed banks to ensure the arrangement runs smoothly, he added.

Sri Lanka’s designation forms part of a wider expansion of China’s clearing network this year. The PBOC authorised Bank of China’s London branch as the UK’s RMB clearing bank in February, a month before the Colombo branch. It has since named clearing banks for Indonesia in June and Frankfurt in August.

title: China Merchants, SLPA, Access scrap $ 392 m logistics hub | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:19
-     - 179

China Merchants Port Holdings Company Ltd., the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA), and Access Engineering PLC have agreed to abandon the South Asia Commercial and Logistics Hub (SACLH) project in Port of Colombo. Under the settlement, the three partners will get back about $ 29.8 million of the $ 37.1 million they had invested.

The Hong Kong-listed port operator said last week that the parties had signed a settlement agreement. The agreement ends the Shareholders Agreement, the Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) Agreement, and the Site Lease Agreement early, and settles all matters relating to the project with immediate effect.

The Daily FT reported in April 2023 that the investment in the project was $ 392 million, when agreements for the hub were signed in Colombo. The project was billed at the time as the largest commercial and logistics complex in South Asia. It was a public-private partnership to be built in the centre of Port of Colombo, with 530,000 cubic metres of storage capacity in an eight-floor building. It was to be developed as a 50-year BOT project. Under that model, a private investor builds and runs an asset for a fixed period before handing it back to the State.

The project company, SACL, is 70% owned by China Merchants Port’s wholly-owned subsidiary FCGL, while Access Engineering and the SLPA hold 15% each. According to SACL’s audited financial statements as at 31 December 2025, the shareholders had contributed $ 37.1 million in cash: $ 26 million from FCGL and $ 5.6 million each from Access Engineering and the SLPA.

Under the settlement, the SLPA has agreed that a $ 26 million investment made by SACL’s shareholders is payable to them, after deductions for tax and late payment liability. The SLPA has already paid a value added tax (VAT) liability of $ 3.9 million to the Inland Revenue Department and will move to settle a further $ 195,000 in late payment liability. The SLPA will pay the remaining $ 21.9 million to SACL as a one-time lump sum within 30 days of the date of the settlement agreement.

SACL will also distribute about $ 7.85 million in cash, which its audited accounts showed as distributable at the end of 2025.

Both sums will be shared in proportion to shareholdings. FCGL will receive about $ 20.8 million, and Access Engineering and the SLPA will receive about $ 4.5 million each. FCGL will therefore recover about $ 5.2 million less than its $ 26 million contribution, and Access Engineering about $ 1.1 million less than its $ 5.6 million.

China Merchants Port said it had reassessed the project in view of changes in external circumstances. These included adjustments to the project’s implementation environment and timetable, as well as the parties’ respective commercial considerations. It concluded that ending the project would be in the best interests of all parties. The settlement was proposed after discussions with the Government, on the principles of ‘amicable consultation and neutral handling.’

The company’s Board, including its Independent Non-Executive Directors, said the terms were normal commercial terms, fair and reasonable, and in the interests of shareholders as a whole.

The partners will now take steps to strike off or, if applicable, wind up SACL. They will share the related costs in the same 70:15:15 ratio.

Under Hong Kong’s Listing Rules, the SLPA counts as a connected person of China Merchants Port at the subsidiary level. This is because the SLPA also holds 15% of Colombo International Container Terminals (CICT), which manages Port of Colombo’s South Terminal and in which China Merchants Port holds the remaining 85%. The settlement is therefore a connected transaction. However, all of the transaction’s applicable percentage ratios are below 1%, so it is exempt from reporting, announcement, and independent shareholder approval requirements. Early termination of the original agreements does require disclosure.

title: We are not inflation nutters; SL not ready for sub-5% inflation target: CBSL | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:17
-     - 273

Senior Deputy Governor Dr. Chandranath Amarasekara – Pic by Ruwan Walpola

The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) has ruled out a lower inflation target for now. It concluded that a goal below 5% would force a prolonged period of tight monetary policy on an economy still recovering from crisis and exposed to repeated external shocks.

CBSL Senior Deputy Governor Dr. Chandranath Amarasekara set out the reasoning behind the new Monetary Policy Framework Agreement (MPFA) in the most detail yet. He said the CBSL had examined whether a target of 2%, 3%, or 4% would suit the current structure of the economy. “The answer was no. We are not there yet,” he said.

The MPFA was signed on 1 October by President and Finance Minister Anura Kumara Dissanayake and CBSL Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe. It retains the 5% target for quarterly headline inflation for the next three years, with an accountability margin of ±2 percentage points. That margin is the band outside which the CBSL must formally account for missing its target. The CBSL’s announcement at the time listed only broad considerations, including economic structure, historical evidence, and international practice.

The decision followed months of debate. Independent economists and Former Finance Minister Ravi Karunanayake had urged a cut to 2% or a 2%-3% range, arguing that a lower target would better protect household purchasing power and strengthen policy credibility.

Dr. Amarasekara spoke at The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce’s Sri Lanka Economic and Investment Summit (SLEIS) 2026 last week. He was responding to a question on why the CBSL had not chosen a lower target that could bolster both household resilience and investor confidence.

He said inflation averaged 12% from the opening of the economy in 1978 to the end of the conflict in 2009. It averaged 11% up to the formal adoption of inflation targeting in 2023. Inflation briefly fell below 5% after the new Central Bank Act took effect, but the record showed Sri Lanka to be a high-inflation economy, and high inflation tends to be volatile, he said.

“Compared to that history, I think 5% is a good inflation rate. It is an ambitious rate, and compared to global best practices, 5% can also be considered low and stable inflation,” Dr. Amarasekara said.

He said around 15 inflation-targeting central banks have targets of about 2%, but 13 of them are advanced economies and only two are emerging markets. Countries exposed to large energy and food shocks typically set higher targets and wider bands. Sri Lanka belongs in that group, he said, given repeated food, energy, and weather shocks beyond the CBSL’s control. Economies that began with high targets, among them Indonesia, the Philippines, Brazil, and the Czech Republic, took close to 20 years to bring them down to around 2%, he added.

At home, he said inflation currently stood at 8% due to the energy shock. Bringing it down to a lower target would require sacrifice: a strict monetary policy regime, and therefore high interest rates, maintained for longer than usual.

“Is this the time to do it? Not really. The economy is facing multiple shocks, and at the same time, we are still recovering from the crisis,” he said.

The CBSL also tested whether a more ambitious target would be welfare-maximising, meaning whether it would deliver the best overall outcome for households and the economy. It found that it would not.

“We are not inflation nutters. We do not want to reduce inflation to extremely low levels at any cost. That is not how we operate, and that is why we are called a flexible inflation targeter,” Dr. Amarasekara said. “Inflation nutters” is a central banking term for policymakers who pursue low inflation to the exclusion of growth and jobs.

His remarks come as the CBSL projects headline inflation to remain in the high single digits through the first quarter of 2027 before easing towards the target, according to CBSL Economic Research Director Dr. L.R.C. Pathberiya.

Dr. Amarasekara did not rule out a lower target in future. “Gradually, I think it would be good for Sri Lanka to move to a lower inflation target, but not right now,” he said. He added that there was no promise as to when, as any move would depend on further analysis.

title: Sri Lanka must earn FTAs, says Deputy Minister | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:15
-     - 75

Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe – Pic by Ruwan Walpola

Sri Lanka must earn free trade agreements (FTAs) through deep domestic reforms rather than expect them to follow from negotiation alone, Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe said.

The Government is now moving to dismantle import levies left untouched for two decades and is seeking entry into Asia’s largest trade bloc.

“We only talk about FTAs, but FTAs don’t come automatically. You have to earn them, and to earn them, you have to carry out a significant level of reforms in your country,” Abeysinghe said at The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce Sri Lanka Economic and Investment Summit last week.

With a small domestic market, Sri Lanka’s growth must come from integration into global value chains, he said, making market access a precondition for investment. 

“Why would foreign direct investment (FDI) come to Sri Lanka if we can’t trade with other nations? Our market is so small,” Abeysinghe said. Some global companies operate locally, he added, but that was not enough.

Two barriers have kept Sri Lanka out of FTAs, he said. The first is the country’s two para-tariffs, the CESS and the Ports and Airports Development Levy (PAL), which are charged on imports on top of Customs duties. The Government plans to remove them by 2029. “For the last two decades, we did not touch it,” he said. He described the change as a reform other countries undertook in the 1980s and 1990s.

Opening the market requires groundwork, Abeysinghe said. Local industries must be strong enough to compete, standards must be enforced to create a level playing field, and anti-narcotics practices must be in place. His Ministry is driving these initiatives alongside the Trade Ministry and the Finance Ministry. The Government is also moving to a simplified four-band tariff structure and improving the efficiency of ports, Customs, and revenue structures. “These are fundamentals that we missed over decades,” he said.

Sri Lanka is now in a position to negotiate, Abeysinghe said. It has applied to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), which he said would open up 30% of the global market, including Australia and New Zealand. It is also close to reaching agreement on the Thailand FTA. Negotiations will start soon to upgrade the goods-only Indo-Sri Lanka FTA into a comprehensive trade agreement, and talks on a possible agreement are underway with Oman and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). In Europe, the Government is working to retain the EU’s Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP+) trade concessions but will have to negotiate a separate trade agreement, he said. With the US, it has managed the existing trade arrangements.

Abeysinghe was blunt about where Sri Lanka can compete. “We can’t play in volume. That’s very clear. In the future, we can’t play on cost arbitrage. There’s no chance,” he said. Instead, the country must position itself in the upper tier of supply chain partners, whether by supplying talent or manufacturing key components for integration into global markets.

That shift places demands on the private sector as well as the State. Product diversification requires the private sector and the Government to jointly invest in research and development to create intellectual property and new products, Abeysinghe said. Barriers to capital repatriation, which have kept venture capital and private equity out of the startup ecosystem, will be removed this year, he added.

He also urged local businesses to seek partnerships with global companies. “We should be bold enough to go and shake hands,” he said. The Government wants hundreds of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to be partner-ready. Most local firms, however, remain private companies, which global investors find hard to assess and approach, and listed companies are few. To address this, the Government plans to encourage mid-sized SMEs to list, and his Ministry will run a program to identify gaps that prevent local firms from forming global partnerships.

Abeysinghe said Sri Lanka is within two and a half hours of a population of 3.3 billion but has traditionally failed to capitalise on that location. Its trade strategy will rest on ports and maritime activities: bunkering, re-exports, and intraport trade. The Colombo, Hambantota, and Trincomalee ports will serve as strategic assets. 

He said Sri Lanka would be ready to partner with the rest of the world within the next two to three years.

title: Tourism earnings rise  for second month, but YTD revenue falls 9.2% | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:14
-     - 105

Sri Lanka’s tourism earnings recorded a second consecutive month of year-on-year (YoY) growth in September, rising 1.5% to $ 185.6 million despite a marginal decline in arrivals, but cumulative revenue remained under pressure amid weaker visitor numbers and continuing external headwinds.

The latest Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) data showed that September’s earnings improvement followed a 2.1% increase in August to $ 264.4 million, ending a 10-month run of YoY declines. Tourist arrivals, however, fell 0.3% in September, extending the disconnect between visitor volumes and foreign exchange receipts.

Despite the recent improvement, cumulative tourism earnings in the first nine months of 2026 declined 9.2% to just over $ 2.24 billion, from $ 2.47 billion in the corresponding period last year.

Arrivals during January to September totalled over 1.69 million, down 1.8% YoY, highlighting the challenge facing the sector as it attempts to regain momentum ahead of the crucial winter travel season.

The performance comes against a backdrop of heightened geopolitical uncertainty following the escalation of Middle East tensions after US and Israeli strikes on Iran from 28 February, which has placed additional pressure on Sri Lanka’s tourism industry.

The latest earnings figures also complicate comparisons with previous years following a revision to the country’s tourism expenditure estimates.

In August 2025, the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) reduced its estimate of average daily tourist spending to $ 148 from $ 171, replacing the estimate based on a 2018 survey. The adjustment lowered the level of tourism earnings recorded from August 2025 onwards, making comparisons with previously published figures less straightforward.

Nevertheless, the earnings trajectory presents a significant challenge for the Government’s revised 2026 tourism targets.

In August, Sri Lanka raised its arrival target to 2.7 million from 2.5 million, while increasing the annual tourism revenue goal to $ 4.2 billion from $ 3.5 billion. These targets followed earlier downward revisions from initial ambitions of 3 million arrivals and $ 5 billion in earnings amid the Middle East crisis.

With cumulative earnings at just over $ 2.24 billion by end-September, the country would need to generate around $ 1.96 billion during the final three months to meet the $ 4.2 billion target. That would require average monthly earnings of around $ 653 million in October, November, and December — substantially above the levels recorded in recent months.

The scale of the challenge is also evident when measured against the sector’s performance last year. Sri Lanka generated $ 3.22 billion in tourism earnings in 2025, up 1.6% from $ 3.17 billion in 2024, while arrivals increased 15.1% to a record 2.36 million from 2.05 million.

The recent return to monthly earnings growth offers a limited positive signal, but the persistent decline in cumulative receipts underscores the difficulty of converting visitor arrivals into stronger foreign exchange earnings.

title: Dialog cedes Doc990 control as Sunshine buys 22% for Rs. 375 m | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:14
-     - 156

Dialog Axiata PLC has given up control of Digital Health Ltd., operator of the Doc990 digital health platform. It sold a 20% stake to Sunshine Holdings PLC’s healthcare arm and Nawaloka Hospitals PLC for Rs. 374.9 million, partially monetising its investment, the companies said on Friday.

Dialog’s wholly-owned subsidiary Digital Holdings Lanka sold 16.65% of Digital Health to Sunshine Healthcare Lanka Ltd., for Rs. 312.2 million. It sold a further 3.35% to Nawaloka Hospitals for Rs. 62.7 million after Nawaloka exercised its right of first refusal under the existing Shareholders’ Agreement, which entitles existing shareholders to buy shares before they are sold to an outsider.

Sunshine Healthcare also acquired the entire 5.26% stake of Ceylon Hospitals PLC (Durdans Hospital) for Rs. 98.7 million.

Durdans exercised its tag-along rights under the Shareholders’ Agreement dated 28 January 2021, which allow a minority shareholder to sell on the same terms when a stake changes hands.

The three sales were priced at Rs. 83.31 a share, valuing Digital Health at Rs. 1.87 billion.

The deals take Sunshine Healthcare’s total outlay to Rs. 410.8 million for a 21.92% holding. That makes it Digital Health’s second-largest shareholder after Digital Holdings, whose stake falls to 27.57% from 47.57%.

Including the 17.09% held by Dialog Axiata Digital Innovation Fund Ltd., the Dialog Group’s total holding falls to 44.66% from 64.66%. Digital Health will cease to be a subsidiary of the Group. Its retained interest will be accounted for as an associate in the Group’s consolidated financial statements, Dialog said.

Nawaloka Hospitals’ stake rises to 12.12% from 8.77%. Asiri Hospital Holdings PLC (13.33%) and Aartiz Technologies Ltd., (7.98%) retain their holdings.

Dialog said the transaction introduces Sunshine Healthcare as a strategic healthcare partner. It is expected to support Doc990’s growth by combining the platform’s digital healthcare capabilities with Sunshine Healthcare’s presence across pharmaceuticals, healthcare distribution, manufacturing, and retail.

Sunshine Holdings said the acquisition would expand its healthcare portfolio and strengthen the Group’s presence across the pharmaceutical, healthcare distribution, manufacturing, retail, and digital health sectors.

title: Vidullanka wins $ 1.35 m Fiji mini hydro contract | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:13
-     - 61

Vidullanka PLC has won a $ 1.35 million contract to build a mini hydro power facility in Fiji, its first foray into the Pacific island region’s renewable energy sector, the company said on Friday.

The company received the Letter of Acceptance on 13 October from Fiji’s Department of Energy under the Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Ministry. A Letter of Acceptance is the formal notice that a bid has been successful, ahead of signing the contract. Vidullanka submitted its bid on 18 December 2025.

The contract covers the design, supply, installation, testing, and commissioning of a 100 kW mini hydro facility at Buca Village on a turnkey Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) basis. Under such an arrangement, the contractor delivers a completed, ready-to-operate project.

Vidullanka said it would complete the procedural and administrative formalities required under the tender conditions before signing formal contract agreements with the Department of Energy. It will make further disclosures once the agreements are executed.

The award builds on the Group’s record of international EPC execution in Guyana in South America and in East Africa. It also reinforces its strategy to diversify revenue into foreign currency-denominated EPC and specialised technical engineering service contracts, Vidullanka said.

Media Services, the publisher of leading business magazine LMD, unveiled the top 20 line-up in its forthcoming LMD 100 annual edition with Hayleys retaining the lead, followed by John Keells Holdings (JKH) and LOLC Holdings.

The 33rd edition of Sri Lanka’s pioneering listed company rankings presents an encouraging picture of corporate performance in the financial year 2025/26. The 100 leading listed companies collectively recorded an increase of approximately 20% in revenue, signalling stronger business activity among key contributors to the national economy.

Hayleys secures the top spot for the third consecutive year with its consolidated revenue exceeding Rs. 585 billion, marking a 19% increase over the preceding financial year. JKH climbs from fifth to second place with a top line of nearly Rs. 529 billion – an increase of 67% – while LOLC Holdings occupies third position with revenue surpassing Rs. 429 billion, up 26%.

Commercial Bank of Ceylon (ComBank) advances three places to fourth with a consolidated revenue of over Rs. 365 billion, followed by Carson Cumberbatch in fifth position with nearly Rs. 349 billion. title: Generator failure triggers islandwide blackout; probe launched into grid collapse: NSO | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:12
-     - 77

The National System Operator (NSO) yesterday said a generator failure triggered an islandwide blackout on Saturday (17), collapsing the country’s national power grid within 30 seconds and prompting an investigation into the sequence of events. The outage occurred at around 11:43 a.m., with the operator noting that a generator’s automatic disconnection under abnormal conditions should not ordinarily cause a complete system collapse.

In a statement issued, it noted that restoration began shortly after the outage, with the main hydroelectric generators reconnected by 12:11 p.m. and the system restarted across four sections. Essential services, including major hospitals, water treatment plants, and airports, had their electricity restored by 3 p.m., while all grid substations were reconnected by 5 p.m., restoring supply to most consumers.

The Norochcholai coal-fired power plant is expected to remain offline for several days, removing 810 MW of capacity from the grid. The NSO stated maximum hydropower generation, supported by prevailing rainfall, and relatively lower demand should help maintain supply with minimal disruption, while an internal investigation examines the cause of the grid collapse.

title: Indian business delegations visit Sri Lanka to explore trade, investment opportunities | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 04:57
-     - 67

Two 10-member business delegations from India, representing the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and the Cochin Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CCCI), visited Colombo to participate in the Sri Lanka Economic and Investment Summit 2026, organised by The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce on 12-13 October. 

The visits provided an opportunity to explore trade and investment opportunities in Sri Lanka, strengthen business-to-business (B2B) linkages, and promote greater economic engagement between India and Sri Lanka.

The CII delegation, comprising representatives from diverse sectors including healthcare and pharmaceuticals, solar energy, information technology, manufacturing, and footwear, held a series of meetings with key stakeholders in Sri Lanka. These included Energy Minister Anura Karunathilaka, Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Deputy Minister Chathuranga Abeysinghe, and senior officials of the Board of Investment (BOI) and Export Development Board (EDB) of Sri Lanka. Discussions focused on investment opportunities, trade prospects, and potential business collaborations across sectors of mutual interest.

The CCCI delegation, representing sectors such as healthcare, logistics, building materials, business consultancy, information technology, and tourism, also held a series of engagements with Sri Lankan stakeholders. The delegation met Deputy Minister Abeysinghe and senior officials of the BOI. The delegation also held B2B meetings with various Sri Lankan companies to explore potential business partnerships and opportunities for collaboration. As part of its visit, the delegation toured the manufacturing facilities of Nestlé and Elephant House to gain first-hand exposure to industrial operations in Sri Lanka.

Both delegations also called on Indian High Commissioner Santosh Jha. During the interactions, the High Commissioner shared his perspectives on the Sri Lankan economy and the growing opportunities for Indian businesses in Sri Lanka. He encouraged the visiting companies to deepen their engagement with Sri Lankan counterparts, establish business partnerships, and explore opportunities for trade and investment.

The visit of the CCCI delegation also forms part of the High Commission’s ongoing efforts to strengthen economic and commercial engagement with Sri Lanka at the regional and sub-national levels, by facilitating greater interaction between regional business chambers and enterprises from different parts of India and their Sri Lankan counterparts. In this context, it may be recalled that business delegations from the South Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SGCCI) and the Tamil Nadu State Council of the Indian Chamber of Commerce (ICC) had also visited Sri Lanka earlier this year. 

The CCCI and The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce also signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the sidelines of the Sri Lanka Economic and Investment Summit 2026 to strengthen trade and business cooperation between Kerala and Sri Lanka. The MoU was signed by CCCI Past President and Executive Committee Member C.S. Kartha and The Ceylon Chamber of Commerce President Krishan Balendra. The MoU envisages enhanced business engagement, with a view to promoting closer commercial ties and mutually beneficial business opportunities.

The visits of the two delegations underscore the continued efforts to strengthen India-Sri Lanka economic and commercial ties through enhanced B2B engagements and institutional partnerships.

title: 1,000 highnetworth Rotarians to gather in Sri Lanka in December for Rotary Institute 2026 | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 04:56
-     - 62

Rotary International will convene its Rotary Institute 2026 in December in Colombo, drawing over 1,000 highnetworth members, including District Governors, past Governors, and senior private sector business personalities from South Asia. 

The conference will welcome Rotary International World President Yinka Babalola and a galaxy of influential personalities from the hierarchy of the Rotary International team from the US, and other representatives from corporate India, said the Rotary Institute Communique.

“Many of the delegates, who are business leaders arriving from overseas, will be firsttime visitors to Sri Lanka — and [this] is a sizeable opportunity that we must not miss,” said Rotary Institute 2026 Chairperson Gowri Rajan, who was responsible for bringing Rs. 120 million for setting up the first Human Heart Valve Bank in Sri Lanka and gifting it to the Lady Ridgeway Hospital (LRH), Health Ministry.

Rajan said central to its agenda is Sri Lanka tourism and investment into the country must be linked to the private sector – tourism and strategic philanthropy.

This signature event of Rotary will be staged at Colombo City Resort property, City of Dreams, Cinnamon Life, and pre-Institute events will be held at Anantara Kalutara. 

Organisers have secured 1,400 roomnights for delegates. The program will feature global best practices, stories of heroic deeds will be featured at the three-day highlevel panels, and targeted networking opportunities designed to catalyse philanthropic partnerships, private investment, and sustainable tourism development in Sri Lanka, said the Communique.

The Rotary Institute 2026 was launched in New Delhi last November at the previous institute, which was attended by the Vice President of India and featured a performance by Cinnamon Life Brand Ambassador Yohani.

Rotary’s global network has a long record of addressing complex challenges, from public health initiatives and polio eradication partnerships to community development and health projects implemented by clubs and districts worldwide. The Rotary Institute 2026 in Colombo is expected to leave a durable legacy of partnerships, projects, and strengthened links between Sri Lanka and Rotary’s global network.

The inaugural ceremony will be graced by Chief Guest Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya.

After 21 years, the Rotary Institute is returning to Sri Lanka, which will be convened by Rotary International Vice President Muruganandam (MMM).

Details of top speakers and partnership opportunities will be announced in the near future, the Communique said.

title: Former diplomat Dhammika Kumari Semasinghe joins Alumex Board | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 04:55
-     - 123

Dhammika Kumari Semasinghe

Alumex PLC has appointed Sriyanee Dhammika Kumari Semasinghe to its Board as an Independent Non-Executive Director.

Semasinghe, a former ambassador and career diplomat, has extensive bilateral and multilateral diplomatic experience gained over 29 years in the Sri Lanka Foreign Service. During her tenure, she promoted Sri Lanka’s diverse interests in the Republic of Poland, New York, Washington, DC and New Delhi.

Her multilateral work at the Sri Lankan diplomatic missions in Washington, DC and New York included liaising actively with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. In New York, she also represented Sri Lanka’s interests in selected Main Committees of the UN General Assembly.

At the Foreign Ministry, she gained nuanced regional and country-specific insights while serving in the Divisions of Europe and Central Asia, South Asia and SAARC, Economic Affairs, UN and Human Rights, and East Asia and the Pacific.

Her professional and academic experience, including training, has broadened her perspective on global developments and trends. It has also given her substantive exposure to policy development, strategic planning, negotiations, networking, lobbying, image promotion and crisis management.

She began her undergraduate studies at the University of Peradeniya before being awarded a full scholarship to Swarthmore College, USA. Semasinghe holds an MA in International Public Policy (MIPP) from the School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS), Johns Hopkins University, Washington, DC, USA, and a BA from Swarthmore College, Pennsylvania, USA.

title: Supreme Court grants leave to former Deputy Minister  in bribery conviction appeal | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:10
-     - 31

The Supreme Court has granted special leave to appeal to former People’s Alliance Deputy Minister Shantha Premaratne, who is challenging his conviction for accepting a Rs. 50,000 bribe to secure employment for a supporter’s son-in-law at the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB).

A three-judge bench comprising Justices Achala Wengappuli, Arjuna Obeysekara, and Gihan Kulathunga granted leave on the question of whether the evidence presented at the trial established the offence for which Premaratne was convicted.

Premaratne was convicted by the Colombo High Court in 2017 and sentenced to eight years’ rigorous imprisonment, with the sentences to run concurrently. The Court of Appeal upheld the conviction in November 2024, prompting him to appeal to the Supreme Court.

The bribery allegation relates to an incident said to have occurred in December 2007, when Premaratne was serving as the Sri Lanka Freedom Party’s (SLFP) Ampara District Leader and Party Organiser. He was accused of accepting Rs. 50,000 from a party supporter in return for arranging employment for her son-in-law at the CEB. Premaratne maintained that the money received was part of donations made by party members towards the construction of the party headquarters in Ampara. He contended that the building had been constructed with the blessings of the party leadership in Colombo.

He also claimed that the complaints against him were instigated by political rivals following his defeat at the 2008 Provincial Council Election and defections from the United National Party (UNP) to the United People’s Freedom Alliance (UPFA) at the time.

Premaratne served as a Deputy Minister under the Chandrika Bandaranaike Kumaratunga-led People’s Alliance Governments between 1994 and 2001, holding portfolios including Tourism and Aviation, Irrigation and Water Resources Management, and Plan Implementation and Parliamentary Affairs. He lost his parliamentary seat in 2001 and was subsequently appointed the SLFP’s Ampara District Leader and Party Organiser in 2005.

Counsel Hafeel Farisz, instructed by Sanjeewa Kodithuwakku, appeared for Premaratne, while Additional Director General Ruvini Wickramasinghe appeared for the Bribery Commission.

title: Court of Appeal issues notice in WNPS challenge to Mannar wind power project | Daily FT
summary:
Monday, 19 October 2026 05:10
-     - 76

The Court of Appeal has permitted a writ application filed by the Wildlife and Nature Protection Society of Sri Lanka (WNPS) to proceed, and has directed that notices be issued on the Respondents. The application challenges the approvals granted for the Phase 1 Extension of the Thambapavani Wind Power Project on Mannar Island. 

The order was made on 31 August, after the application was supported before the Court on 9, 16, and 27 July and 3 and 4 August. The Court has ordered the objections of the noticed Respondents to be filed, whilst notices are due to be served on the parties who have now taken over the work of the former Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB).

The WNPS contends that the relevant authorities failed to comply with mandatory provisions of the law when approvals were granted for the project, and that this failure risks irreversible consequences both for the communities living on Mannar Island and for its fragile ecosystem in an area regarded as one of Sri Lanka’s most ecologically important regions.

The application seeks judicial intervention in respect of what the WNPS considers to be serious violations of regulations made under Sri Lanka’s environmental laws. The Society contends that the wind turbines are being constructed in unapproved locations, and that the number of turbines is well in excess of the number approved by the relevant regulatory authority. It challenges the implementation of the project on the basis that the statutory procedures required under, among other legislation, the National Environmental Act and the Coast Conservation and Coastal Resource Management Act were not complied with.

The Society has raised particular concern over the failure to adhere to the findings of the Avifaunal Study commissioned by the Project Proponent itself. According to the WNPS, that study identified certain areas within the project zone as presenting a “very high” risk to bird populations. The WNPS alleges that, despite these findings, turbines have been installed in areas identified as high-risk or prohibited zones. The Society says this could increase the threat to migratory and endangered bird species and intensify pressure on an already sensitive ecosystem, with significant risks also to sensitive coastal habitats and to the livelihoods of the communities living in the area.

Mannar Island forms part of the Central Asian Flyway, a major migratory route used by millions of birds each year. The island has been recognised by national and international experts as a Key Biodiversity Area and as a site of global importance for water birds. It also lies close to several protected areas, including the Vankalai Sanctuary, the Vidataltivu Nature Reserve, and the Adam’s Bridge Marine National Park.

The proceedings therefore seek to place before the Court the question of whether the project has been implemented in accordance with Sri Lanka’s environmental laws and the safeguards intended to protect environmentally sensitive areas.

The WNPS has stressed that it fully supports renewable energy and Sri Lanka’s transition to cleaner sources of power. Its challenge is directed at the failure of the authorities and regulators to comply with the law and with the recommendations of the regulatory authorities themselves. The Society maintains that renewable energy projects must be located and developed in accordance with environmental safeguards and the law, and that the case is ultimately about ensuring that Sri Lanka’s renewable energy transition proceeds in a manner that is both legally compliant and environmentally sustainable, particularly in locations of exceptional ecological importance.

The WNPS was represented by President’s Counsel Farzana Jameel, with Attorneys-at-Law Prashanthi Mahindaratne, Dilumi de Alwis, Manisha Dissanayake, and Minaz Izzadeen, instructed by Attorney-at-Law Dilini Jayasuriya.
